notes.title: Next Closed Beta: June 27 to 30
notes.content:
[h3]A huge thank you to everyone who joined us in May. Your feedback has helped us squash bugs, tweak balance, and polish the experience. We can't wait to see you back in the game!
[/h3]

[h3]Now, onto the last 6 Zodiacs…
[/h3]

[h2]The Zodiac Animals: Meet the Final Six Signs
[/h2]

[h3]The zodiac cycle is made up of twelve animals, each with its own traits and personality. We've already covered the first six—now let’s shine a spotlight on the rest! Do you share a zodiac sign with one of these legendary creatures?[/h3]

[h2]🐴 The Horse
[/h2]Free-spirited and full of adventure, the Horse is known for its energy and determination. If you were born in 1978, 1990, or 2002, you share the sign of this passionate and ambitious traveler, always ready to chase their dreams.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/7a9a948c5b6211751f9afbe3da072398fcc7a9f3.png[/img]

[h2]🐐 The Sheep[/h2]
Born in 1979, 1991, or 2003? Your zodiac sign is the Sheep! Gentle, creative, and compassionate, Sheep have a deep appreciation for art and beauty, making them thoughtful and kind-hearted individuals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/5f9c23d38014806365b5c96851a35d93206bc08c.png[/img]

[h2]🐵 The Monkey
[/h2]Witty, playful, and full of energy, Monkeys are the life of the party. If you were born in 1980, 1992, or 2004, you share a sign with this clever and mischievous creature who always finds a way to succeed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/6a75e76fc379d3e4c65c31df46bbd63c48aac221.png[/img]

[h2]🐔 The Rooster
[/h2]Born in 1981, 1993, or 2005? You’re a Rooster—hardworking, confident, and always up for a challenge! Roosters are known for their sharp minds, strong sense of responsibility, and eye for detail.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/045816b2ea5fd1fc1e8c118e002fdf0c452dc218.png[/img]

[h2]🐶 The Dog
[/h2]Loyal, honest, and protective—Dogs are natural friends and guardians. If you were born in 1982, 1994, or 2006, you share a sign with this devoted and courageous companion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/090c99f141c9fd45cdffc4901744dcbf28df586b.png[/img]

[h2]🐗 The Pig
[/h2]Born in 1983, 1995, or 2007? Your zodiac sign is the Pig! Pigs are kind, generous, and easygoing, known for their warm hearts and strong sense of responsibility. They bring joy and loyalty to those around them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/936fd4bd6016ee0ce22d0b1e551bbfe84102cef2.png[/img]

A big thank you to everyone who joined us during this Beta period! We received lots of valuable feedback and had an amazing time watching your streams and games of Lunars. It was so exciting to see the community come together and share in the fun!
We can’t wait to show you what’s coming next!

Now that we’ve covered all twelve zodiac animals, which one do you relate to the most? 
🐉🐍🐯🐰🐭🐂🐴🐐🐵🐔🐶🐗

notes.title: Lunars Closed Beta: May 23–26! 🚨
notes.content:
[h3]We’re back with another weekend of plushie-powered chaos! The May Closed Beta runs from May 23 to 26, and it’s packed with familiar fun and exciting new features.[/h3]

[h2]Returning Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] 4 wild boards to outsmart your friends (or enemies)
[*] 30+ minigames to win, lose, and absolutely scream over
[*] 3 game modes, including the fast-paced, no-wait Blitz Mode
[*] Online multiplayer and local co-op so you can play together wherever you are
[/list]
[h2]New in May[/h2]
[list]
[*] New outfits to dress up your plushies in style
[*] A brand new emote system (starting with our expressive dragon!)
[*] Early support for custom game settings so you can tweak matches your way
[*] Visual updates to several minigames
[*] New language support: Traditional Chinese, Polish, and Hungarian
[*] General improvements based on your April feedback including UI polish, improved stability, and early host migration support (still in testing)
[/list]
[h2]How to play[/h2]
If you played in April, you’re already in! Just update your build when the beta goes live on May 23.

[b]If you're new:[/b]
[list]
[*] Sign up on Steam for a chance to join
[*] Wishlist the game to support us
[*] Join our Discord for updates and bonus beta key drops
[/list]
[h2]Share Your Best Moments![/h2]
Caught a chaotic minigame moment? Emoted at the perfect time? We’d love to see it!
Share your clips in the #clips channel on Discord or tag us on socials. We’re making another recap video and might feature your gameplay (with credit, of course)!

[h2]Wishlist & Leave a Demo Review[/h2]
We're a small two-person team, and every bit of support helps. If you're enjoying Lunars, review the demo and don't forget to wishlist the game on Steam. It boosts visibility and means the world to us as we work toward launch!

notes.title: Happy Lunar New Year from Lunars! 🎊🐍
notes.content:
[h1]Happy Lunar New Year from Lunars! 🎊🐍[/h1]

[h2]The Year of the Wood Snake is here! To celebrate, we're introducing a special Wood Snake skin—slither into the festivities in style! 🐍✨
[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/d3259723dd9a5f6e127c934f1d2e997573958520.jpg[/img]

The Lunar New Year marks a time of renewal, reflection, and celebration, and what better way to honour it than by exploring the Chinese Zodiac? The zodiac cycle is made up of twelve animals, each with its own traits and personality. We're shining a spotlight on six of these legendary creatures—do you share a zodiac sign with one of them?


[h2]🐍 The Snake 
[/h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/48ffb8fe0383ebe3fc9c34b17a60e1122caabeeb.jpg[/img]
Born in 1989, 2001, or 2013? Your zodiac sign is the Snake! Known for being wise, intuitive, and sophisticated, Snakes are natural strategists who approach life with careful thought and charm.

[h2]🐲 The Dragon
[/h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/b94f2320da745c0cd8f915a05911c6ca1313156b.jpg[/img]
The fifth animal in the cycle, Dragons are confident, charismatic, and dynamic. Born in 1988, 2000, or 2012? You share the sign of this legendary creature, often seen as a symbol of strength and luck.

[h2]🐰 The Rabbit
[/h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/8abca2f92a7f6f6e6a79d2403e1037b9255e00c6.jpg[/img]
Born in 1987, 1999, or 2011? You’re a Rabbit—gentle, quick-witted, and graceful. Rabbits bring kindness and harmony wherever they go, making them beloved among friends and family.

[h2]🐯 The Tiger
[/h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/121e348907d5292c340f72b2e8ab8daf9d55b0a7.jpg[/img]
Tigers are bold, courageous, and confident, always ready to take on new challenges. If you were born in 1986, 1998, or 2010, you share the fierce and determined spirit of the Tiger!

[h2]🐂 The Ox
[/h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/fa97a78fd75353030afeebb0df95444a55a3c20c.jpg[/img]
Dependable and hardworking, the Ox represents resilience and perseverance. If you were born in 1985, 1997, or 2009, your sign is the Ox—strong, steady, and always ready to put in the effort.

[h2]🐭 The Rat
[/h2][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/b1f96f23f793366a78a4aa8f5ba385d5c9497a28.jpg[/img]
The very first animal in the Chinese Zodiac, the Rat is known for its cleverness, charm, and resourcefulness. Born in 1984, 1996, or 2008? You share a sign with the cunning creature who outsmarted them all to take the top spot!

[h2]Wishing you prosperity, happiness, and good fortune in the year ahead! 💖[/h2]

As we step into the Year of the Wood Snake, we want to thank our amazing community for being part of this journey! Which zodiac sign do you belong to? Let us know in the discussion and join us in celebrating this festive season! 🎉🐉🐰🐯🐂🐭

notes.title: Characters Devlog
notes.content:
[h1]Characters[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/a885b6fd52211eb6f991e56ad542e55c68d5114e.png[/img]

We are coming to you with another Devlog! This time, we want to talk about character and customization. I hope you will have a great time reading, and let’s jump into it!

[h3][b]The Inspiration Behind Zodiac Characters[/b][/h3]
When we set out to create the characters for Lunars, we knew we wanted something both familiar and unique—something that matched the fun, mischievous spirit of party games. The 12 Lunar Zodiac signs were perfect for this. They’re rich in history, globally recognized and full of cheeky, quirky personalities that we could have a ton of fun reimagining. Picture a Toy Story-like backdrop where these Zodiac animals are turned into little plushies with attitude. Now they’re off causing mischief when no one’s looking, bringing just the right amount of chaos to the party.

[h3][b]New Characters: What’s Next?[/b][/h3]
Are we adding more characters in the future? Well, let's just say the lore surrounding the Lunar Zodiac animals is incredibly rich. Each country has its own variation on the Zodiac, which means there’s plenty of room for new ideas. So while I can neither confirm nor deny anything, it’s safe to say the ground is fertile for future character development if we choose to pursue it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/5c0f9b2033565dcce8c0fce43a9b3f736a4281bd.png[/img]

[h3][b]Customization: Where Are We Going?[/b][/h3]
Customization is a huge part of making a character feel like it’s truly yours. Right now, we’re focusing on offering players. accessories and skins to mix things up. As Lunars evolves, we’ll explore more options—think more outfits, unique auras, elaborate skins, and unlockable features that let players express their unique style. We want customization to grow with the game and give you all the tools to make your Zodiac plushie uniquely yours.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/c36994d6fbc8285a5d3aa514f9380741ee606460.png[/img]

[h3][b]Exclusive Outfits: Will They Be a Thing?[/b][/h3]
One question we’ve been getting a lot is whether each character will have exclusive outfits. For now, that’s more the exception than the rule, but we’re always listening to player feedback. Exclusive outfits give us more creative freedom since we don’t have to make them fit every character. But we also understand the desire to use an outfit across multiple characters. Some might get their own specific looks, but overall, we want to offer a wide range of customization options so everyone can find something they love.

[h3][b]Skins: Elemental and Beyond[/b][/h3]
We’re really excited about skins, especially now that we’ve started rolling them out. Each character will have skins representing the five elements—Earth, Wood, Fire, Water, and Metal. But that’s just the beginning. We’re experimenting with even more ideas, and we’re keeping an eye on community feedback to see what players want. Down the line, we might introduce more elaborate outfits that completely transform a character’s look, as Lunars continues to grow.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/6b304929ab49a0f72d800f339dd097026336425b.png[/img]

[h3][b]Character Progression: Leveling Up?[/b][/h3]
Many players have asked about the possibility of leveling up characters individually. While it’s something we’re considering for the future, for now, experience points (EXP) will go into a shared pool. This keeps the gameplay straightforward and accessible without adding too much complexity early on. We want to make sure everyone can enjoy the game without worrying about advanced progression systems—at least to start.

[h3][b]Join the Conversation[/b][/h3]
I could talk about outfits and customization all day, but what we really want is to hear from you. After all, what better inspiration for new outfits than the players who will be rocking them? If you’ve got ideas for skins, accessories, or outfits, we’d love to hear them. Join our Discord or Steam community and follow us on social media to stay up to date with all the latest outfit news and updates. We can’t wait to see how you style your Zodiac plushies!

notes.title: Minigames Devlog
notes.content:
[h1]Minigames[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/b443ed8f4f58f7b95f5cd33f68d4503eaaa2bec7.png[/img]

In today’s Devlog, we want to talk about the Minigames  — our thoughts, ideas, and inspirations. We hope that after reading this, you'll understand our take on development!

When it comes to inspiration for *Lunars*, we’ve drawn from every game we—and the Lunars community—have ever played. We’ve got influences from party games like *Mario Party* and *Fall Guys*, console classics like *Pilotwings*, and yes, even *Minesweeper*! The beauty of working on a game like *Lunars* is that it’s like being a kid in a candy store—you can mix and match game concepts, and suddenly, you’ve got a brand-new mini-game or a fresh twist on an old classic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/13e319c3109cc82e4c4b74a80a69336b7ee4f51b.png[/img]

Looking back, it’s hard to pinpoint our “first” mini-game. From day one, we had so many ideas bouncing around that it felt (and still feels) like a brainstorming session with a hundred caffeinated squirrels. If I had to choose, we might’ve started tinkering with Water Wheel first, but it could have just as easily been Penguin Posse or Slice of Life. Honestly, it’s all a bit of a blur!

One thing we’ve learned from playtesting with the Lunars community is that different players excel at different genres, which makes some mini-games feel easier for some than others. We wanted the basics to be accessible enough for anyone to pick up and play, but we also built in higher-skill ceilings so hardcore players could get their fix. We’re always listening to player feedback, and we’ve got the option for mini-game variants. So, if a particular mini-game difficulty is driving people nuts, we can split it into a harder and easier version. Our goal is to make sure everyone’s having a blast, even if it means tweaking the challenge level.

When it comes to team mini-games, we’ve explored a bunch of ideas. We’ve got 2-player teams cooperating to reach a goal, 4v4 setups like in Soccer Punch, asymmetrical setups where one group is more powerful but has fewer players, team captures where one team starts off smaller but can convert the other team’s players, and elimination teams where eliminated players come back with the goal of taking out the remaining players. It’s all about variety and keeping things fresh and exciting!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/7c23d09f07ab33ad7f2a7e5bbefc2bf2a83c350e.gif[/img]

As we head into early access, we’re aiming to have at least 25 mini-games in *Lunars*, and by launch, we’ll be in the 30s. We’ll continue to add more based on what you, the players, think. Being a small team has its challenges, but it also gives us the creative flexibility to respond to our players and explore some of the more unconventional ideas. And trust me, if there’s one thing we have plenty of, it’s fun mini-game concepts just waiting to come to life.
Now, about a scoreboard at the end of mini-games, showing the best scores of last week or month—while we don’t have that built into the game yet, it’s something we’re definitely considering. We see the value in it, but it needs careful handling since *Lunars* is a party game, and your score could be heavily impacted by your co-players helping you out—or, you know, sabotaging you. We want to keep the fun and competition balanced.

One last thing before I go—we’re making *Lunars* the kind of game you can enjoy with friends, family, or even that random group you meet online. Whether you’re playing online or in person, we’re all ears when it comes to feedback. We’re committed to making *Lunars* as fun as a barrel of monkeys, even if that means tweaking a mini-game after launch. So, keep those suggestions coming—we’re here for it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/76a5bfdfe038b7a2387e5407bfd613877b714bc3.png[/img]

notes.title: Inspiration for the Game Devlog
notes.content:
[h1]Inspiration for the Game[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/f7f20db246d4baa485a2063d80daf46d5bf8bd6d.png[/img]

In today’s Devlog, we want to talk about the Inspiration for the game — our thoughts, ideas, and inspirations. We hope that after reading this, you'll understand our take on development!

Do you know that feeling when you’re ready to dive into a game with friends, only to find yourself waiting for what feels like a lifetime for someone to finish their turn? Yeah, we’ve been there. So, we thought, "What if we could make a game that’s all about the action, none of the waiting?" Thus, Lunars was born—where turn-waiting is a distant memory, and you’re always in the thick of it, no matter what. No one likes being eliminated and stuck on the sidelines, so we said, "Let’s keep everyone in the game, always."

We pulled ideas from every corner of our gaming lives, whether it was something we played as kids, something our community threw at us, or something that just popped into our heads after one too many late nights. The twist? We make sure even if you’re "out," you’re never really out. It’s all about bite-sized moments of fun that keep you and your friends on your toes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/64028821c94e0869a610f1b374627ce46d5dd7cd.png[/img]

About the characters - Imagine tiny plushies going on epic adventures through worlds that are way too big for them. That’s our vibe. We took a little inspiration from the Mario games and a sprinkle of Little Big Planet added our own plushie flair, and voilà! You’re now exploring miniature worlds with Lunars that look like they just jumped off a toy store shelf.

We thought, “What if the 12 lunar zodiac animals came to life as plushies with their own quirky personalities based on their zodiac?” Then we realized, "Oh no, that’s 12 characters to animate, rig, and bring to life." But hey, who needs sleep… Now, each Lunar has its own character, its own charm, and watching players pick their favorites has made it all worthwhile. Sure, it wasn’t the easiest path, but seeing those plushies in action? Totally worth it.

Our playlist looks like it was made by someone who wanted to include nostalgic classics and the next big thing at the same time. We’re talking Mega Man X, Synthwave, N64 classics, J-pop, Donkey Kong, electro-swing —you name it.. Luckily, we’ve got some insanely talented musicians who took our wild ideas and turned them into the perfect soundtrack for every minigame. It’s like a sonic buffet, with something for everyone.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/0ab8c1defa4baab33143ebd367d998a382390416.png[/img]

About the maps -  Let’s just say we had to do our homework. We hadn’t played as many board games as we had video games, so we hit the books—or rather, the boards. After a few “lively” brainstorming sessions, and maybe a few (more than a few) scrapped ideas, we finally got our unique board designs. The result? Maps that are as fun as they are strategic, with events that keep you guessing.

Enter Hermes, your charming and slightly mischievous shopkeeper who’s always got something up his sleeve. The idea was simple: let players buy items that give them an edge, but also make sure that in Blitz mode, time is money—and getting hit could cost you more than just a few coins. We wanted every item to feel like it mattered, whether you’re playing fast and loose or taking your time.

Outfits are our love letters to the community. We’re always listening on Discord, taking notes on what you guys want to see next. Whether it’s a nod to pop culture or just something that makes you smile, we’re all about adding new looks that let you express yourself—and look ridiculously cool while doing it.
I can’t wrap this up without giving a huge shout-out to our community. You’ve been our biggest inspiration, our loudest cheerleaders, and sometimes our harshest critics (that’s a compliment… we need that). Thanks for sticking with us and helping us make Lunars something special. We couldn’t have done it without you.
It’s also no secret that Mario Party has been a massive source of inspiration for us. But instead of just following in its footsteps, we’ve made it our mission to create something truly unique with Lunars. We’ve put in the work—late nights, endless debates—to carve out a special little corner for Lunars in the party game universe. Every step of the way, we’ve been hell-bent on making sure Lunars brings something fresh to the party, something that stands out with its own quirky, one-of-a-kind vibe.

See you in the next Devlog!

notes.title: Local Multiplayer Devlog
notes.content:
[h1]Local Multiplayer[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41838134/4686cee52f527902b209e468a4fe0f5fe760f7af.png[/img]

In today’s Devlog, we want to talk about Local Multiplayer—our thoughts, plans, and why it's so important to us. We hope that after reading this, you'll be inspired to try it out with your friends!

From the very beginning, creating a local multiplayer experience was one of our primary goals. We wanted to bring the classic party game feel to 'Lunars,' where friends and family can gather around and enjoy playing together on the same screen. The social interaction and fun that come with local multiplayer were key aspects we wanted to capture.

Local multiplayer is incredibly valuable to us. It's a core feature that defines the spirit of 'Lunars.' We believe that the best gaming moments often happen when players are physically together, sharing laughs, strategies, and sometimes even friendly rivalries. Having local multiplayer ensures that Lunars can create those memorable experiences that bring people closer.

One of the main challenges was ensuring that the game remained balanced and fun regardless of the number of players. We had to carefully design the mini-games and board mechanics to work seamlessly whether there were two or four players. We also put a lot of effort into optimizing the user interface and controls for multiple players on a single screen to ensure the experience is smooth and enjoyable for everyone.

Lunars supports up to four players in local multiplayer. We aimed to create a true party game experience for groups of friends and family. The game is great for both children and adults, making it perfect for family events. Our playtesters range from 10 years old upwards and include both hardcore and non-gamers to ensure the experience is suitable for everyone.

Lunars also allows up to four local players to join online players, for a total of up to eight players in a single game. This feature ensures that you can enjoy the game with friends and family at home while also connecting with others online for a truly inclusive multiplayer experience.

We focus heavily on playtesting with groups of different sizes, ages, and dynamics. This helps us identify any balance issues or areas where the fun might dip. We also keep an eye on community feedback to understand what players enjoy most and continuously refine the game to enhance those aspects. Blitz mode is great for parties because we know turn-based gameplay isn't for everyone, and you want to cater to everyone's enjoyment at a party.

We’re constantly listening to the community on what makes the game fun for both local and online multiplayer. We are always discussing ideas and ways to overcome challenges, such as how we might add support for more players locally in a meaningful way without impacting the experience. Your feedback is essential in helping us make Lunars even better!

It is also worth mentioning that Lunars has support for most controllers and mouse+keyboard. Players have the flexibility to choose their preferred control method.

One thing I’d like to add is a big thank you to our community. Your feedback and enthusiasm are what drive us to keep improving and adding new features to 'Lunars.' We’re excited to continue this journey with you and can’t wait to hear about the fun moments you have playing together. Stay tuned for more updates and keep the suggestions coming!

See you in the next Devlog!
